controls.label: MATISSE reconstruction
controls.notes: An image of the photosphere reconstructed by the public SQUEEZE code from public VLT/MATISSE visibilities and closure phases of 8 and 19 February 2020, in the 3.94-4.00 micrometre continuum, convolved to the 4 milliarcsecond interferometric beam and cast onto a sphere of the published radius, so nothing finer than the beam is shown. Negating every closure phase fits equally well, so which limb is brighter is weakly constrained. The colours are a legend for reconstructed relative intensity in one infrared band, the paper's heat scale: not colour, temperature or albedo. The faint halo outside the disc is the same reconstruction's light beyond the photosphere, a fifth of the flux: half of it within one beam of the limb, the rest extended emission the visibilities require. The far hemisphere and the poles were not observed.
